history.dynasty: Legendary origins (Ramayana); expanded under the Vijayanagara Empire; modern complex developed by philanthropist R. N. Shetty (20th-21st century)
history.period: Ancient shrine; 123-ft Shiva statue standing since 2006; 249-ft Raja Gopura inaugurated 2008
history.summary: Per legend, Murudeshwara is where the cloth covering of Ravana's Atma Linga fell on Kanduka Hill - Ravana was tricked by Ganesha into grounding the linga at Gokarna (worshipped as Mahabaleshwara), and the scattered fragments formed the pancha-kshetra shrines around Gokarna. The ancient Shiva temple on Kanduka Hill, surrounded on three sides by the Arabian Sea, was later expanded under the Vijayanagara Empire. The modern landmark complex was developed by businessman and philanthropist R. N. Shetty: the 123-ft Shiva statue (built by Shivamogga's Kashinath and other sculptors for about Rs 50 million, taking about two years, standing since 2006 - ranked the second or third tallest Shiva statue in the world depending on whether the Statue of Belief and Kailashnath Mahadev are counted), the 249-ft 20-21-storey Raja Gopura with a lift (inaugurated 2008), and the Bhukailasa cave museum with a light-and-sound show beneath the statue. The complex also houses shrines to Ganesha, Vishnu and Parvati.

name: Murudeshwara Temple
town_description: Murudeshwar (Murudeshwara) is a coastal town in Bhatkal taluk of Uttara Kannada district, Karnataka, on the Arabian Sea coast along NH-66, about 155-165 km south of Mangaluru. Built on and around the Kanduka Hill, which juts into the sea on three sides, it is both a major Shiva pilgrimage centre and a beach tourism destination, and lies on the Konkan Railway line.

travel.road: On NH-66 (Mumbai-Goa-Mangaluru); ~155-165 km from Mangaluru, ~100 km from Udupi, ~78 km from Gokarna.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maha Shivaratri (February-March) for the grand festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-1:00 PM and 3:00-8:00 PM (some sources report 8:15/8:30 PM close; darshan 6:30 AM-12:30 PM and 3:30-7:30 PM - verify)
